description: A cursor loop RECORD cannot be bound into EMBEDDED SQL by name. Live-verified inside FOR r IN c DO ... END FOR: :r.price is a SYNTAX ERROR at the dot, a bare r.price is invalid identifier 'R.PRICE', a bare r is invalid identifier 'R', and :r alone is 'Bind variable :r not set.'. Frostlake used to substitute only the :r part of :r.price and leave NULL.price in the SQL, so the documented-looking spelling silently inserted NULL instead of the field value - which is why the decisive assertion here is that NOTHING WAS WRITTEN, not merely that an error was raised. The idiom Snowflake does support is copying the field into a variable first and binding THAT, which sums to 30. The field itself reads fine in a procedural EXPRESSION, because an expression is not embedded SQL. And the regression guard that goes with all of it: src:a.b inside a loop body is a semi-structured PATH, not :a followed by .b. Converted 1:1 from scripting/RecordFieldBindFormTest (now retired); the Java walked the whole cause chain to find the message, which messageContains covers directly.

steps.sql: DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT 10 AS price UNION ALL SELECT 20; BEGIN FOR r IN c DO INSERT INTO bind_out VALUES (:r.price); END FOR; RETURN 1; END
DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT 10 AS price UNION ALL SELECT 20; pv INTEGER; BEGIN FOR r IN c DO pv := r.price; INSERT INTO bind_ok VALUES (:pv); END FOR; RETURN 1; END
SELECT v FROM bind_ok ORDER BY v
DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT 10 AS price; n INTEGER DEFAULT 0; BEGIN FOR r IN c DO n := r.price + 1; END FOR; RETURN n; END
DECLARE c CURSOR FOR SELECT 1 AS n; BEGIN FOR r IN c DO INSERT INTO bind_variant_out SELECT src:a.b FROM bind_variant; END FOR; RETURN 1; END
